title: What If Your Dad Was Mike Tyson?
tags: what if your dad was mike tyson
description:
Imagine you're eleven, pinned against a locker by the biggest kid in school. Then the hallway goes quiet. Your dad just walked in. And your dad is Mike Tyson. 🥊

Twelve rounds of growing up as his son, and every round is scored: the perks or the price. A limo to fight night, a front-row seat, a tiger named Biscuit and a roof full of pigeons… and 4 a.m. runs, a chicken breast for a birthday cake, no right to quit. Then a nine-foot green giant challenges your father to one last fight.

Would you want Mike Tyson as your dad? Tell us in the comments 👇

title: What If You and Your Crush Got Stuck in an Ice Cave?
tags: what if you got stuck in an ice cave
description:
▶ NEW VIDEO: What If Your Dad Was Mike Tyson? https://youtu.be/NyECEbdzT7Y

You're on Mount Everest at sunrise, roped to your crush. Then you hear a sound like a train. 🏔️

The ground opens and the mountain swallows you both: an ice cave deep inside the glacier. No sky. No signal. Minus fifteen degrees. The radio is dead, the search is called off, the meltwater takes a bag, and now there's only one sleeping bag. Seven days under the ice: a frozen squirrel with an acorn, goodbye videos for home, the truth you never told her… and one ice axe.

Would you dig, or wait for rescue? Tell us in the comments 👇

title: What If Men and Women Lived on Different Planets?
tags: what if men and women lived on different planets
men are from mars women are from venus
description:
What if men and women got so tired of arguing that every woman on Earth moved to Venus and every man moved to Mars? One night in 2067, four hundred million couples couldn't agree where to eat. The next morning, the world voted to split up.

Floating cloud cities with eleven pillows on every couch. Lava-tube man caves with a TV on every wall. Brunch and book clubs against beer, football and a barbecue that won't light on a planet with no oxygen. Then a dust storm swallows Mars, the batteries start running out, and the men have to do the one thing they never do: ask for help.

Would you move to Venus, to Mars, or stay on Earth and pick dinner yourself? Tell us in the comments 👇

title: What If This Video Has 26,746 Views?
tags: what if this video has views
description:
What if every view of this video was a person waking up? Almost everyone on Earth sits in a chair inside an Elppa helmet, watching an endless feed, and the number in the title counts everyone who got out.

Sam lived on a dump in Pittsburgh until lightning fried his helmet and he looked around for the first time in three years. Forty days alone, hunted by the red drones of Closed IA, until he found thousands of broken helmets that could still upload and recorded this video. A nurse, a mechanic in Lagos, a whole dump in São Paulo, a midwife in Seoul… and the views, subscribers, likes and comments under this video decide how far they get.

If you could say one thing to someone who's still asleep, what would it be? Tell us in the comments 👇

What if real life became an RPG overnight? Everyone gets a level, a class and dungeon doors all over the city — and you're level one, the lowest in town.

You're a twenty-five-year-old night guard. Overnight, a floating tag appears above every head: nurses are Healers, couriers are Rogues, and you are LV 1 · class NONE. Falling inside sends you back to level one — but you're already there. Moss trolls, sand golems, a frost wyvern, legendary loot… and a giant door in the museum that only lets in one person.

What if you and your crush were the last two people on Earth, in a zombie apocalypse where they hunt by sight, smell and sound? And you're the loudest guy in the building.

Three weeks ago, eight billion people turned. Now it's just you, the sound guy from 6A, and Nora, the night-shift nurse from 5A who left fourteen notes on your door asking you to please be quiet. Then she leaves you one more. To survive, you'll raid a supermarket in a storm, take the guns from a police station, steal a truck from a military checkpoint and break into the hospital where it all began, while six new kinds of zombies hunt you: the Shrieker, the Juggernaut, the Leapers, the Mimic, the Stalker and the Titan. And on day one hundred, eighty thousand of them are waiting at the stadium.

Which one would get you first: the Juggernaut, the Mimic, the Stalker or the Titan? Tell us in the comments 👇

What if you could heal anyone in the world just by touching them? But every heal drains a power bar that never comes back up.

You're twenty-six and you fix cracked phones for a living. One morning a scratch on your arm disappears under your glowing palm. A stray cat's broken paw, a kid at the park, your mom's bad knee, a whole emergency room in eleven minutes… Soon there's a line around the block and the whole world wants one touch. But every heal costs a piece of a bar you can't see. And one day, two people you love will need it to live — with only enough left for one.

If you had one heal left, would you save the people you love, or yourself? Tell us in the comments 👇

title: What If You Were the Only Man on an Island of 100 Amazons?
tags: what if you were the only man on an island
description:
▶ NEW VIDEO: What If You Could Heal Anyone With Your Hands? https://youtu.be/Crah_A8xhhE

What if you were the only man on an island of 100 Amazons? You wash up inside a ring of bronze spears, and you have thirty days to change their minds.

Your little sailboat hit a reef in a storm. The queen gives you one moon. On the thirtieth night, all one hundred warriors vote with their spears: if every spear goes up, you can stay forever; if even one stays down, the sea takes you back. The last man who washed up here, in 1987, got ninety-nine. You can't throw a spear, you can't swim the reef, and you can't make fire without a lighter. But back home you fix things for a living, and this island is about to need you.

Would you stay on the island forever, or go home? Tell us in the comments 👇

title: What If You Were Frozen for 1,000 Years?
tags: what if you were frozen for 1000 years
what if you woke up 1000 years in the future
description:
▶ NEW VIDEO: What If You Were the Only Man on an Island of 100 Amazons? https://youtu.be/UtXsABU4Cek

What if you were frozen for 1,000 years? This what if animation wakes you up in 3026 with a hundred dollars in the bank, a robot that is more scared than you, and a mystery: somebody kept your pod cold on purpose.

It was supposed to be one night. A lab paid you a hundred bucks. A thousand years of compound interest later, you're the richest person in history. Too bad pizza costs fourteen million a slice, nobody understands your English, and the bank would very much like you to be dead. Then you find a note signed J.

So... who would keep your pod cold for a thousand years? Tell us in the comments.

Real facts in this video
• Moss frozen in Antarctic permafrost for over 1,500 years grew again in the lab: Roads, Longton & Convey, Current Biology 24(6), 2014. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cub.2014.01.053
• English from the year 1026 is unreadable today: the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle entry for that year reads "Her for Ælfric biscop to Rome" ("In this year bishop Ælfric went to Rome"), manuscript D.
• In 1790 Benjamin Franklin left 1,000 pounds to Boston and told the city to wait 200 years; by 1990 the fund was worth about $4.5 million: Education Week, April 1990. https://www.edweek.org/education/benjamin-franklins-penny-saved-means-training-dollars-for-2-cities/1990/04
• US consumer prices rose more than 30 times since 1913 (CPI-U 9.9 in 1913, 313.7 in 2024): U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. https://www.bls.gov/cpi/
• The Moon drifts away from Earth by about 3.8 cm a year, measured by bouncing lasers off the Apollo reflectors: NASA. https://eclipse.gsfc.nasa.gov/help/ApolloLaser.html
• Vint Cerf, one of the fathers of the internet, warned in 2015 of a "digital Dark Age": files nobody keeps copying become unreadable: BBC, February 2015. https://www.bbc.com/news/science-environment-31450389

Everyone in this video is fictional.

#whatif #animation #future

title: What If Your School Had to Rebuild Civilization?
tags: what if your school was the last place on earth
what if you were the last person on earth
description:
▶ NEW VIDEO: What If You Were the Only Man on an Island of 100 Amazons? https://youtu.be/UtXsABU4Cek

What if your school was the last place on Earth? This what if animation follows 512 people, one teacher and a row of school buses through the first 100 days of a brand new world.

At ten fifteen in the morning, every person on Earth vanishes. All eight billion, except the 512 people in your school. Past the fence there is no town and no road, just white. The water stops on day three. The power dies on day seven. The food will last nineteen days. But every skill you level up in real life, from rain catchers and bike generators to a greenhouse on the gym roof, laws and even money, makes the world grow back a little. Then the school splits in two.

So... what skill would you bring to restart the world? Tell us in the comments.

Real facts in this video
• A person pedaling hard keeps up roughly 75–100 watts of mechanical power: https://mathscinotes.com/2014/11/the-limits-of-human-generated-power
• The Svalbard Global Seed Vault held 1,378,238 seed samples at the end of 2025: NordGen Annual Review 2025. https://publication.nordgen.org/NordGen-Annual-Review-2025/svalbard-global-seed-vault.html
• Zimbabwe, November 2008: monthly inflation of about 79.6 billion percent, with prices doubling roughly every 24.7 hours; a Z$100 trillion note followed in January 2009: Steve Hanke, Johns Hopkins Magazine, 2009. https://magazine.jhu.edu/2009/08/27/what-hyperinflation-looks-like
• In 1965 six Tongan schoolboys were stranded on the island of 'Ata for about 15 months and survived by working together: Rutger Bregman, The Guardian, 9 May 2020. https://www.theguardian.com/books/2020/may/09/the-real-lord-of-the-flies-what-happened-when-six-boys-were-shipwrecked-for-15-months
• Robbers Cave, 1954: 22 boys at a summer camp, split into two groups, turned hostile; shared goals such as fixing the camp's water supply brought them back together: Muzafer Sherif et al., Intergroup Conflict and Cooperation: The Robbers Cave Experiment (1961). http://psychclassics.yorku.ca/Sherif/
• Astronauts on the International Space Station talk to schools by amateur radio (ARISS); the 1,000th contact was on 10 March 2016: https://www.arrl.org/news/ariss-marks-its-1000th-contact

Everyone in this video is fictional.

#whatif #animation #survival

title: What If You Could See Everyone's Search History?
tags: what if you could see everyone's search history
description:
▶ NEW VIDEO: What If You Were the Only Man on an Island of 100 Amazons? https://youtu.be/UtXsABU4Cek

What if you could see everyone's search history? This what if animation gives you five days: every morning, the search bar above everyone's head shows a little more. First their last search, then the whole day, the whole week, the deleted ones, and finally incognito.

Imagine you wake up on Monday, and there's a search bar above everyone's head. Max, two meters of muscle: how to make friends when everyone is scared of you. Chloe, the most popular girl in school: how to look like I don't care. And Ava? Ava searched you.

But there's a catch: you start making money from what you read. And on Friday at noon, it flips. The whole school sees yours.

Along the way, the real side of search: why so many searches are brand new, how "anonymous" searches exposed a real person in 2006, what incognito actually hides, and how long deleted history really takes to disappear.

So... if everyone could see your search history, what would they find? Tell us in the comments.

Real facts in this video
• About 15% of the searches Google sees every day are new, never typed before. Google has repeated this figure since 2013: https://searchengineland.com/google-reaffirms-15-searches-new-never-searched-273786
• Curiosity as the pain of an information gap: Loewenstein, Psychological Bulletin 116(1), 1994. https://doi.org/10.1037/0033-2909.116.1.75
• In 2006 AOL released about 20 million searches from about 650,000 users; reporters identified user No. 4417749 from her searches alone: The New York Times, 9 August 2006. https://www.nytimes.com/2006/08/09/technology/09aol.html
• Search data as a "digital truth serum": Seth Stephens-Davidowitz, Everybody Lies (2017).
• Deleted data is removed from view right away, but fully deleting it from Google's systems generally takes around two months: Google, How Google retains data we collect. https://policies.google.com/technologies/retention
• In 2024 Google agreed to destroy billions of private browsing records to settle the Brown v. Google lawsuit over incognito mode (filed 1 April 2024): https://abc7news.com/post/google-lawsuit-incognito-searching-browsing-history-third-party-cookies/14606586/

Everyone in this video is fictional.

#whatif #animation #searchhistory

title: What If You Could See Who Loves You?
tags: what if you could see who loves you
how to tell if someone likes you
how to tell if a girl likes you
who has a crush on you
description:
▶ NEW VIDEO: What If You Were the Only Man on an Island of 100 Amazons? https://youtu.be/UtXsABU4Cek

What if you could see who loves you? This what if animation gives you three days of hearts above everyone's head: who hates you, who doesn't care, and who loves you 100%.

Imagine you wake up tomorrow, and there's a heart above everyone's head. Black means they don't like you. Gray means you don't matter to them. Red means they like you. And 100% means they're in love with you.

But there's a catch: day one, you only see black hearts. Day two, gray. Day three, red. Then they vanish for a whole year. Your best friend turns out to be at −100%. And the person who loves you 100% is the last person you'd ever guess.

Along the way, the real science of how to tell if someone likes you: a real smile versus a polite one, pupils that widen, and why believing someone likes you can make it come true.

So... whose heart would you check first? Tell us in the comments.

Real facts in this video
• A real smile usually also tightens the muscles around the eyes (the "Duchenne smile"), a polite one often only moves the mouth: Ekman, Davidson & Friesen, Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 58(2), 1990. https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.58.2.342
• Social circles come in layers of about 5, about 15 and about 150 people: Zhou, Sornette, Hill & Dunbar, Proceedings of the Royal Society B 272(1561), 2005. https://doi.org/10.1098/rspb.2004.2970
• People who were led to believe a partner liked them behaved more warmly, and the partner came to like them more: Curtis & Miller, Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 51(2), 1986. https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.51.2.284
• Mutual gaze between dogs and their owners raised oxytocin in both: Nagasawa et al., Science 348(6232), 2015. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1261022
• About two thirds of cats tested (64% of kittens) were securely attached to their owners, close to the share seen in human infants: Vitale, Behnke & Udell, Current Biology 29(18), 2019. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cub.2019.08.036
• Pupils tend to widen when we look at something or someone we find interesting or pleasant: Hess, Scientific American 212(4), 1965. https://doi.org/10.1038/scientificamerican0465-46

Everyone in this video is fictional.

#whatif #animation #love

title: What If You Were Invisible?
tags: what if you were invisible for a day
what if you could turn invisible
what if you could stop time
what if you could become invisible
description:
▶ NEW VIDEO: What If You Were the Only Man on an Island of 100 Amazons? https://youtu.be/UtXsABU4Cek

What if you were invisible for a day? This what if animation follows 24 hours of invisibility: the best day of your life, then everything goes wrong.

Imagine you wake up tomorrow, and you're invisible. Not a costume. Not a trick. Completely invisible.

For a few hours, it's the best day of your life: free coffee, first class, courtside at the NBA Finals, a vault full of gold and the Oval Office. Then you walk into a women's locker room, and everything goes wrong. By midnight, the whole city is hunting you. And at 11:59, you find out the one thing every invisible person would lose.

Would you still want to be invisible? Tell us in the comments.

Real facts in this video
• Below about 27 °C a resting naked body has to spend extra energy to stay warm (estimates of this lower critical temperature run 27–30 °C): Speakman & Keijer, Molecular Metabolism 2(1), 2013. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.molmet.2012.10.002
• Airport body scanners don't need light: millimeter-wave scanners build their image from radio-frequency energy reflected off the body. DHS, Privacy Impact Assessment Update for TSA Advanced Imaging Technology. https://www.dhs.gov/sites/default/files/publications/privacy-tsa-pia-32-c-ait.pdf
• In England and Wales, voyeurism (watching someone undress without their consent, for sexual gratification) carries up to 2 years in prison: Sexual Offences Act 2003, section 67. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2003/42/section/67
• Food takes about 6 hours on average to move through the stomach and small intestine (the often-quoted range is 6–8 hours): Mayo Clinic, Digestion: How long does it take? https://www.mayoclinic.org/digestive-system/expert-answers/faq-20058340
• Dogs have up to 300 million olfactory receptors in their noses, people about 6 million: PBS NOVA, Dogs' Dazzling Sense of Smell (2012). https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/nova/article/dogs-sense-of-smell/
• Normal body temperature is about 37 °C (98.6 °F): MedlinePlus, Body temperature norms. https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/001982.htm. Thermal cameras see that heat as long-wave infrared, and ordinary window glass blocks it.
• To see, your retina has to absorb light. An eye that light passes straight through absorbs nothing, so a truly invisible person would be blind.

Everyone in this video is fictional.

#whatif #invisible #animation

title: What If Humans Never Invented Clothes?
tags: what if humans never invented clothes
description:
▶ NEW VIDEO: What If You Were the Only Man on an Island of 100 Amazons? https://youtu.be/UtXsABU4Cek

You wake up tomorrow, open your closet... and there's nothing in it. Not even socks. In this world, humans never invented clothes.

So we walked through seven rooms of that world: the cold, the sun, the office, the awkward part, the missing industry, space... and the morning Kevin had an idea.

Would you survive one day in this world? Tell us in the comments.

0:00 A world without clothes
0:42 Room 1: The Cold
2:35 Room 2: The Sun
4:03 Room 3: The Office
5:31 Room 4: The Awkward Room
6:30 Room 5: The Missing Industry
7:47 Room 6: Space
8:32 Room 7: The Idea
9:23 The Exit

Real facts in this video
• Clothing is roughly 170,000 years old: body lice, which live in clothes, split from head lice around then. Toups et al., Molecular Biology and Evolution 28(1), 2011. https://doi.org/10.1093/molbev/msq234
• Below about 27 °C a resting naked body has to spend extra energy to stay warm (estimates of this lower critical temperature run 27–30 °C): Speakman & Keijer, Molecular Metabolism 2(1), 2013. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.molmet.2012.10.002
• Earth's average temperature is about 15 °C: NASA Earth Fact Sheet. https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/earthfact.html
• Unprotected skin can be damaged by the sun in as little as 15 minutes: CDC, Sun Safety. https://www.cdc.gov/skin-cancer/sun-safety/
• More than 100 billion garments were made in 2014, nearly 14 for every person on Earth: McKinsey & Company, Style that's sustainable (2016). https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/sustainability/our-insights/style-thats-sustainable-a-new-fast-fashion-formula
• Richard Arkwright patented his water-powered spinning frame in 1769: Encyclopaedia Britannica. https://www.britannica.com/biography/Richard-Arkwright

Kevin, the squirrel and everyone else are fictional. Any resemblance to real Kevins is a coincidence.

#whatif #animation #clothes

title: What If You Got Stuck in the Woods With a Man or a Bear?
tags: would you rather man or bear
bear or man in the woods
description:
▶ NEW VIDEO: What If You Were the Only Man on an Island of 100 Amazons? https://youtu.be/UtXsABU4Cek

You're alone in a forest. Behind one tree, a bear. Behind the other, a man you've never met. You're stuck with one of them until morning.

So we tried both. One of them steals your sandwich. The other one has a podcast.

Bear or man? Tell us in the comments.

0:00 The question that broke the internet
0:55 Option 1: the bear
4:21 Option 2: the man
6:35 So why the bear?
7:33 Plot twist
8:53 Man or bear?

Real facts in this video
• The 2024 street interview where 7 of 8 women picked the bear: Screenshot HQ (TikTok), April 2024. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Man_or_bear
• Bear behaviour and what to do (avoid surprises, don't run, play dead in a defensive grizzly attack, fight back against a black bear): National Park Service, Staying Safe Around Bears. https://www.nps.gov/subjects/bears/safety.htm
• Black bears killed at least 63 people in the US and Canada, 1900–2009: Herrero et al., Journal of Wildlife Management 75(3), 2011. https://doi.org/10.1002/jwmg.72
• About 1 grizzly injury per 3.6 million visits to Yellowstone, 1979–2023: Gunther & Atkins, Ursus 36, 2025. https://doi.org/10.2192/URSUS-D-24-00010R1
• 78% of sexual violence against women in the US (2005–10) involved someone the victim knew: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Female Victims of Sexual Violence, 1994–2010 (2013). https://bjs.ojp.gov/library/publications/female-victims-sexual-violence-1994-2010
• The YouGov poll (US adults, 6–7 May 2024, n = 6,245): 40% of women picked the man and 31% the bear; 21% of men picked the bear. https://yougov.com/en-us/daily-results/20240507-ca5c4-2

Kevin, Gerald the bear and the squirrel are fictional. Any resemblance to real Kevins is a coincidence.
